study type: Retrospective study of prospectively collected data
cohort: 384 infants (4 twin pairs) with gestational age ≥32 weeks born to 380 CMV IgG positive/IgM negative mothers
finding: Breastfeeding and vaginal delivery were associated with increased postnatal CMV infection rates, but CMV infection did not appear to negatively affect growth or liver enzymes in term or late preterm infants.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a higher CMV infection rate compared to Cesarean section.
